title: Wolves in Yellowstone National Park
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2026 Grade 5 ELS Released Items, Questions 10-13
directions: Base your answers to questions 10 through 13 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: In the 1800s, wolves were commonly found from the cold Arctic regions to Mexico. By the early 1900s, almost no wolves were found in the United States because of habitat loss and hunting by humans.

In 1973, the northern Rocky Mountain wolf was listed as an endangered species. As a solution, wolves were reintroduced into the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem. From 1995 to 1997, 41 wild wolves from other areas were released into Yellowstone National Park.
Wolves are highly social animals. They eat a wide variety of prey, both large and small. They mate in February, and females give birth to an average of five pups in April.
At the end of 2022, there were 108 wolves in Yellowstone. These wolves lived in 10 different packs, ranging in size from 4 to 25 wolves.

coatColor.html: In Yellowstone, about half of the wolves are black in color, and the other half are gray in color.
Studies of these wolves have shown the following:

items: Gray-colored wolves are more aggressive than black-colored wolves during encounters with other wolf packs.
The litter sizes of gray-colored wolves are slightly larger than the litter sizes of black-colored wolves.
Wolves often choose mates of the opposite color.
Black-colored wolves have a greater survival rate from some diseases than gray-colored wolves.

items.stem: Which fact does not support the argument that being part of a wolf pack helps members survive?
options: The leading cause of death for wolves outside Yellowstone Park is humans.
Food and protection is provided to newborn pups.
Large prey are hunted and killed by wolves.
Regions in which wolves live are defended from other wolves.

items.stem: Which statement correctly summarizes what the studies found comparing wolves with different coat colors?
options: Wolves have traits that can be influenced by the environment.
Variations in characteristics of wolves may provide advantages in surviving and reproducing.
Traits of wolves are inherited from parents, and variations of these traits exist in a pack.
Internal structures of wolves allow for survival, growth, and successful reproduction.

items.stem: Identify one food source for the white-tailed deer in Yellowstone National Park. Then, describe how this food source would be affected if the white-tailed deer population changed when more wolves were introduced into the park. Include a reason for this change in your description. [1]

parts.label: Effect on food source:
parts.exemplar:
The cottonwood (or willow) would probably increase because more deer would be killed by the wolves, so the deer would not be eating the plants.
OR
There would be more willow (or cottonwoods) because less deer would be eating them due to more wolves eating more deer.
OR other valid response

rubric: Cottonwood or willow is chosen as the food source.
A description that the food source would increase is provided. (A description implying that the food source would increase is also sufficient.)
A reason for this increase is provided. (A reason that is minimally provided, as when it must be inferred that the deer eat the cottonwood, is also sufficient.)
No credit: A description that the cottonwood “would not go down as fast” is ambiguous and does not imply an increase in the food source due to a disruption to the ecosystem.
No credit: A description that the food source would “changce” does not imply an increase.
No credit: A description that the food source would increase with no reason for this increase, such as “There would be more cottonwood for elk and beavers to eat.”
items.exemplar:
Food source: cottonwood/willow
Effect on food source: The cottonwood (or willow) would probably increase because more deer would be killed by the wolves, so the deer would not be eating the plants. OR There would be more willow (or cottonwoods) because less deer would be eating them due to more wolves eating more deer. OR other valid response

items.stem: Which piece of evidence from the graphs supports the claim that wolves are dependent on elk for their survival in Yellowstone National Park?
options: From 2010 to 2017, both the wolf and elk populations decreased, then increased.
Both the wolf and elk populations increased from 2005 to 2006.
From 2000 to 2004, the number of wolves increased while the number of elk decreased.
The highest wolf populations were in 2004 and 2008, while the highest elk populations were in 1995 and 2000.
